title: Interteam dependency catalog and autoresolve rules for quarterly roadmaps
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Cross-functional initiatives (Eng/Design/Security/Infra) frequently miss handoffs because ownership and conditional fallthroughs aren’t captured in a single canonical place. This ticket scopes a lightweight interteam dependency catalog and a set of machine-evaluable 'autoresolve' rules that can reduce manual coordination for low-risk blockers and surface high-risk blockers to leads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Catalog schema defined and accepted by Eng/Design/Security leads; 2) Autoresolve rules prototype implemented that can mark a dependency as 'auto-cleared' or 'requires-review' based on SLA and impact tags; 3) Two pilot initiatives authored in the catalog (runtime batching and console rollout) with automated notifications wired to Slack; 4) Metrics dashboard showing time-to-clear and manual escalations before and after pilot.
milestones: 2025-02-07 to 2025-02-14: Discovery interviews with Eng, Design, Security, Infra
2025-02-15: Catalog schema v0.1 published in Confluence
2025-02-18: Autoresolve rule engine prototype (feature-branch) merged to staging
2025-02-22: Pilot onboarded (2 initiatives) and alerts wired to #roadmap-ops
2025-03-10: Evaluate pilot and decide on org-wide rollout
updates: 2025-02-10 — Scoping: scoped to catalog schema + rule primitives (SLA, owner, fallback, impact, mitigation notes). Agreed to keep initial rule language intentionally conservative (only low-impact, infra-config and documentation tasks eligible for autoresolve).

2025-02-13 — Trade-offs: Eng raised concerns about false positives for autoresolve. Decision: require a cooldown window (48h) and a 'last-updated-by-owner' check before auto-clearing. Logged as rule exception case.

2025-02-15 — Schema published: Confluence doc created with fields: dependency_key, owning_team, owning_person, impact_level, sla_hours, fallback_path, resolution_artifact_link, allowed_autoresolve (boolean), notes. Feedback requested from Security for sensitive infra dependencies.

2025-02-18 — Prototype: PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap-tooling/pull/318) with rule engine that evaluates on cron and emits events to a staging webhook. Initial run filtered 14 historical blockers; 9 flagged as candidate-for-autoresolve, 5 required manual review.

2025-02-20 — Pilot onboarding: runtime-batching (ENG-9120) and console-rollout (PM-4092) added to catalog. Slack flow posts summary alerts to #roadmap-ops and pings owners when an autoresolve candidate appears.
2025-02-22 — Blocker: Need security sign-off for any dependency that touches encryption/KMS; added explicit security_review_required flag for those items.
2025-02-22 — Next step: Build a small Linear integration to attach catalog entries to tickets and surface the 'allowed_autoresolve' state in the ticket sidebar.
comments: Asha Patel (2025-02-11): Good first pass — please include an 'escalation_contact' field in the schema.
Diego Morales (2025-02-13): Will implement the cooldown and last-updated checks. Also +1 to conservative defaults.
Marta Singh (Security) (2025-02-15): Need to ensure any autoresolve path is logged and auditable. Recommend adding 'resolution_artifact_link' and immutable audit events.
Leo Park (Design) (2025-02-18): For design handoffs, acceptable autoresolve only if a completed design spec is attached. Otherwise mark as 'requires-review'.
risks: Autoresolve incorrectly clears a blocker causing downstream outages — mitigated by conservative rules and audit logs.
Low adoption if schema requires extra work to annotate tickets — mitigate with Linear sidebar integration and a small data-migration script.
Security pushback for infra items — addressed by explicit security_review_required flag and manual review paths.
rollout_plan: Pilot (2 initiatives) for 4 weeks -> measure time-to-clear and manual escalations -> refine rule whitelist -> enable for low-impact infra and docs tasks org-wide -> ship Linear sidebar + dashboard. Rollback: disable cron job and surface all pending candidate items for manual triage.
